mainTopic: Calculating dates after the חורבן: converting year counts, finding one's place in the שמיטה cycle, and when the גאולה may be close
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's discussion of how to count years. First it gives a פסוק about the 48 cities as a memory aid for the number 48. Then it explains that a scribe (ספרא) who lost track of the year can ask the תנא for his count and subtract 48. Next, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע teaches a method for finding which year of the שמיטה cycle we are in. You add one year, count in יובלות and seven-year cycles, and move two years from every hundred into the leftovers. After that, רבי חנינא and a ברייתא each name a year after which you should not buy land even at a huge bargain. The גמרא lines the two dates up and shows they are only three years apart. Finally, the גמרא begins a story about a certain שטר, and what was written in it comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A memory aid for the number forty-eight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the previous calculation with a פסוק that helps you remember the number 48.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the calculation it was just discussing by giving a פסוק as a memory aid for the number 48.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number 48 is the key gap in the date conversion being taught. To keep it in mind, the גמרא points to the 48 cities of the לויים mentioned in the תורה.

phrases.english: "Forty-eight cities."
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:7. It's a memory trick for the number 48 in the calculation just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the calculation that came right before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The number 48 in the calculation can be remembered through the 48 cities of the לויים.

steps.title: If the scribe forgets the year, he asks the תנא and subtracts forty-eight
steps.stepSummary: A scribe who loses track of the year can ask the תנא for his count and subtract 48 to get the right number.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the scribe makes a mistake, let him ask the תנא how many years he counts, subtract forty-eight from that, and he will find his number. And your memory sign: the scribe subtracts, the תנא adds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reverse rule: if the scribe forgets the date, he can get it from the תנא's count by subtracting 48.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scribe and the תנא use two different counting systems, and the gap between them is 48. So going from the תנא's number to the scribe's number means taking 48 away. The memory sign helps you remember the direction: the scribe's number is smaller, the תנא's number is bigger.

keyTerms.meaning: Scribe, the one who writes dates in documents
The one who recites and teaches the oral traditions

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the direction. The תנא's number is the larger one, so the scribe subtracts from it; the תנא would add to the scribe's number.

phrases.english: And if the scribe makes a mistake —
let him ask the תנא how many years he teaches,
and subtract forty-eight from them,
and he will find his number.
phrases.notes: He means that this way he'll arrive at the correct year.

phrases.english: And your memory sign: the scribe subtracts,
the תנא adds on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse conversion that uses the same 48-year gap.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scribe who lost track of the year takes the תנא's count and subtracts 48.

steps.title: How to find your year in the שמיטה cycle
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a method: add one year, count large blocks as יובלות and the rest as seven-year cycles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע says: Someone who does not know which year of the seven-year cycle he is in should add one year, and then count the large numbers in יובלות and the small numbers in seven-year cycles.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains how to work out which year of the שמיטה cycle it is now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You start from the years since the חורבן and add one, so the count lines up with the beginning of a cycle. Then you break the total into big blocks (יובלות, each made of seven שמיטה cycles) and smaller leftovers (single seven-year cycles).

keyTerms.meaning: The large units, the big numbers
The small units, the leftover numbers

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Someone who does not know
which year of the seven-year cycle he is in —
should add one year,
phrases.notes: Add it to the number of years since the חורבן, so the count starts at the beginning of a cycle.

phrases.english: and count the large numbers in יובל cycles,
and the small numbers in seven-year cycles.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from converting dating systems to working out the שמיטה year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To find the שמיטה year: add one year to the count since the חורבן, then break it into יובלות and seven-year cycles.

steps.title: Adjusting for two extra years in every hundred
steps.stepSummary: From each hundred years, move two years into the leftovers, then divide the leftovers into seven-year cycles. The memory sign is the פסוק about two years of famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he should take two from every hundred, add them to the small numbers, and count the small numbers in seven-year cycles. Then he will know which year of the cycle it is. And your memory sign: "For these two years the famine has been in the land."
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes his method by adding a correction: each hundred years leaves two extra years that must be moved into the leftover count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hundred years is two full יובלות (98 years) plus 2 more. So for every hundred, you move those 2 years into the leftovers and then divide the leftovers by seven. Whatever remains tells you where you are in the current cycle.
steps.whatToRemember: The method: start from the years since the חורבן and add one, take 2 years from every hundred into the leftovers, and divide the leftovers by seven.

phrases.english: And he should take two from every hundred,
and add them to the small numbers,
and count the small numbers in seven-year cycles,
and he will know which year of the cycle it is.
And your memory sign: "For these two years
the famine has been in the land."
phrases.notes: בראשית 45:6. The words "two years" remind you to take two from each hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב הונא's method with the two-per-hundred correction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Move two years from every hundred into the leftovers before dividing by seven.

steps.title: After 400 years from the חורבן, don't buy land even at a bargain
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says that after 400 years from the חורבן, you should not buy a field even for a tiny price.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: After four hundred years from the destruction of the בית המקדש, if someone tells you, "Buy a field worth a thousand dinars for one dinar," do not buy it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: רבי חנינא names a date after which buying land is not worth it, even for almost nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual explanation is that after this point the גאולה could come at any time, and then land would go back to its original owners. So even a huge bargain is not a real gain.

keyTerms.meaning: The destruction of the בית המקדש
Do not buy (literally, do not take)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
After four hundred years from the destruction of the Temple,
if a person says to you:
"Buy a field worth a thousand dinars
for one dinar" — do not buy it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from calculating years to a date that has meaning for the future.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After 400 years from the חורבן, do not buy land even at a huge bargain.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives the same advice with the year 4231 from creation
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule, but dates it from the creation of the world: after the year 4231.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: After the year 4231 from the creation of the world, if a person says to you, "Buy yourself a field worth a thousand dinars for one dinar," do not buy it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same advice as רבי חנינא, but it counts from creation instead of from the חורבן. This sets up the next question about how the two dates compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is almost the same as רבי חנינא's; only the counting system and the number are different. That makes us wonder whether they are really giving the same year.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching from the תנאים outside the משנה

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא:
After four thousand two hundred
and thirty-one years from the creation of the world,
if a person says to you:

phrases.aramaic: קַח לָךְ שָׂדֶה שָׁוֶה אֶלֶף דִּינָרִים
phrases.english: "Buy yourself a field worth a thousand dinars
for one dinar" — do not buy it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel source to רבי חנינא's statement that uses a different counting system.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the year 4231 from creation, do not buy land even at a huge bargain.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two dates?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי חנינא's date and the ברייתא's date differ.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: do these two dates point to the same year or not? It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since one source counts from the חורבן and the other from creation, you can't compare them at a glance. The גמרא wants to line them up and see the gap.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two dates just brought.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How far apart are רבי חנינא's date and the ברייתא's date?

steps.title: The ברייתא's date is three years later
steps.stepSummary: The two dates are three years apart; the ברייתא adds three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference of three years between them, since the ברייתא adds three years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources differ by only three years, and the ברייתא's date is the later one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חורבן was in the year 3828 from creation, so 400 years after it is 4228. The ברייתא says 4231, which is three years more.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא (400 after the חורבן = 4228) and the ברייתא (4231) give nearly the same date; the ברייתא is three years later.

phrases.english: There is a difference of three years between them,
since the ברייתא adds three years.
phrases.notes: 400 years after the חורבן comes out to 4228 from creation, three short of the ברייתא's 4231.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how the two dates differ.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two dates are three years apart; the ברייתא's year is three years later than רבי חנינא's.

steps.title: A story begins about a certain document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a story about a particular שטר and starts to tell us what was written in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain document in which was written...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a story about a real שטר. This line is only a setup, getting us ready to hear what was written in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic so far has been counting years and dates. Now the גמרא moves from rules to a real case. This line names the object of the story, a שטר, and the very next words will tell us what it said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That one' or 'a certain'. This word often opens a story about a specific case.
A document, such as a loan note. Documents like this carry a written date.
'Written in it'. This introduces the exact wording found in the document.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a complete thought. Do not look for a ruling here yet. The content of the document comes in the next words.

phrases.english: There was a certain document
in which was written

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier steps dealt with counting years and comparing dates. This step turns to a real case about a document, where those counting questions come into play.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces the case: a certain שטר and what was written in it.
